title: Optimal Division
statement:
Write the integers of `nums` in their given order with a `/` between every two neighbours. Read from left to right, this expression divides them one after another using exact (real-number) division. You may insert parentheses anywhere to change the order in which the divisions are done. Return, as a string, the expression whose value is as large as possible.

- The string keeps the numbers in their original order and uses only digits, `/`, `(` and `)`, with no spaces.
- It must not contain redundant parentheses: no pair may be removable without changing the order of evaluation (this includes a pair around the whole expression or around a single number).
- If `nums` holds one number, the expression is just that number.
- The input guarantees that exactly one expression gives the largest value.
constraints: Exactly one optimal division exists for the given input.
notes:
## Intuition

However the parentheses are placed, `nums[0]` always ends up in the numerator and `nums[1]` always in the denominator. Every later number could land on either side, and since each one is at least `2`, the value is largest when **all** of them are in the numerator. Grouping everything after the first number does exactly that: `b/c/d` equals `b/(c·d)`, so `a/(b/c/d)` equals `a·c·d/b`. An interval DP that tries every split (the brute force) reaches the same answer in O(n³).

## Approach

1. One number: return it as it is.
2. Two numbers: there is only one expression, `nums[0]/nums[1]`; parentheses would be redundant.
3. Otherwise join `nums[1..]` with `/` into `denominator`; inside it, left-to-right order is already correct, so it needs no inner parentheses.
4. Return `nums[0]` divided by `denominator` in one pair of parentheses.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1000, 100, 10, 2]` has more than two numbers. `denominator = "100/10/2"`, and the result is `"1000/(100/10/2)"`, which evaluates to `1000 · 10 · 2 / 100 = 200`. Other placements are smaller, for example `1000/(100/(10/2)) = 50` because it moves `2` into the denominator.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) to build the string.
- Space: O(n) for the result.

## Pitfalls

- `"2/(3)"` is wrong for two numbers: parentheses around a single number are redundant.
- Nesting more parentheses inside the denominator, like `100/(10/2)`, moves numbers back into the denominator and lowers the value.
- The answer is a string; there is no need to evaluate any division.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums` | the numbers, in their fixed order |
| `denominator` | everything after the first number, joined with `/` |

narration.2: A single number is already the whole expression.
narration.3: Return it as text with no operators.
narration.5: With two numbers there is only one possible division.
narration.6: Parentheses here would be redundant, so write it plainly.
narration.8: Join every number after the first with slashes; left-to-right order inside is already right.
narration.9: Divide the first number by that whole group, which puts every later number except nums[1] in the numerator.
